Like most open-source foundations, the goal of the Django Software Foundation is to promote, support, and advance its open-source project: in our case, the Django Web framework. The foundation's goals are to: Support development of Django by sponsoring sprints, meetups, gatherings and community events. Promote the use of Django among the World Wide Web development community. Protect the intellectual property and the framework's long-term viability. Advance the state of the art in Web development. Corporate Members ¶ The Django Software Foundation would not be able to operate without the generous financial support of our corporate members . If you are interested in becoming a corporate member of the DSF, you can find out more on our corporate membership page Individual Members ¶ Individual members are appointed to the Django Software Foundation in recognition of their contributions to the Django community. If you know of someone that you think should be a member, including yourself, please fill out this form and the DSF membership will enter them into consideration. Support for events The DSF is happy to provide financial and other support to Django events around the world. Find out how the DSF can support your conference or other event . Code of Conduct requirement The DSF will only endorse or support events which publish and adhere to a suitable Code of Conduct . Prizes The DSF awards prizes to recognize the contributions of volunteers in the Django community. pages.title: Django Accessibility Statement | Django
pages.text: Skip to main content Django The web framework for perfectionists with deadlines. Menu Main navigation Overview Download Documentation News Code Issues Community Foundation ♥ Donate Sponsor Search Submit Toggle theme (current theme: auto) Toggle theme (current theme: light) Toggle theme (current theme: dark) Toggle Light / Dark / Auto color theme Django Accessibility Statement Django accessibility statement The Django Software Foundation is committed to fostering an inclusive and accessible community, project, and ecosystem. Accessibility is integral to creating a space where everyone — regardless of ability — can contribute, build, and benefit from the Django framework and its broader community. Our commitment ¶ We strive to make Django itself and its related online and in-person spaces accessible for all. This includes: Supporting the creation of accessible web applications with Django. Ensuring that our documentation, community tools, and websites are navigable and usable for people with disabilities. Encouraging accessibility awareness across all aspects of the project, from events and communication to software design and development. Accessibility in the Django web framework ¶ We aim for conformance with recognized standards such as the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) and the Authoring Tool Accessibility Guidelines (ATAG). Where feasible, we strive to exceed these standards. Through documentation, tutorials, and exemplar implementation, we highlight best practices for building accessible applications. We also encourage feedback and contributions to improve accessibility features in Django’s admin interface and related tools such as Django forms, particularly from people with disabilities or other accessibility needs. Community and events ¶ The Django Software Foundation is committed to ensuring that events receiving our grant funding are accessible to all. We encourage organizers to choose venues and platforms that meet physical accessibility needs, that provide resources such as captioning and sign language interpretation where possible. We welcome feedback to make improvements on any and all aspects of physical accessibility. What we do ¶ Known issues and continuous improvement ¶ We acknowledge that there is always room to improve. Accessibility is an ongoing process, and we aim to address issues as they arise. Known accessibility issues with the Django framework, admin interface, or community platforms are tracked publicly, and we welcome collaboration to resolve them. For further details, see: Issues matching “accessibility” for the Django framework Issues tagged “accessibility” for the Django website Django accessibility improvements kanban Current efforts ¶ The Django accessibility team encourages projects maintained by the Django Software Foundation to be accessible to as many people as possible, particularly those with disabilities that make using the web more difficult. This includes testing with assistive technologies , reviewing changes to Django for accessibility, updating project guidelines and documentation, and publishing reports. How you can help ¶ We invite all members of the community to contribute to accessibility efforts. This could include: Reporting accessibility issues in Django’s admin interface, documentation, or websites. This can also be done on the Django forum in Accessibility . Sharing knowledge, testing, or feedback on accessibility in Django-built projects. Sponsoring or contributing to accessibility-focused initiatives. For more information and opportunities to contribute, consider contacting the Django accessibility team . Feedback and contact ¶ We value your input. If you encounter an accessibility barrier or have suggestions for improvement and none of the above options seem appropriate, please contact the accessibility team. Find us on: Accessibility on the forum , #accessibility on Discord , or if neither work for you please use the Contact us page. Back to Top Django Links

He then tweeted about it . Unfortunately, the changeset in question is enormous (around 21,000 lines in the diff) and attempting to process it causes Django's Trac instance to chew up all of our server's CPU, effectively resulting in the entire djangoproject.com website being unavailable. So for now, requests for that changeset are being redirected here; if you want, you can still browse the Django codebase through Trac or do an SVN checkout to see what's changed. capabilities.note: AG-01 needs local reading of this packet only. AG-02, AG-03, AG-05 and AG-06 need a search tool the host actually ran. AG-04 needs the host to view the full image. A missing capability leaves only its own checks not_assessed.

AG-01.name: About-page concreteness
AG-01.finding_requires: a packet page reference (E...), the exact passage read, and which of who / offering / category it leaves unanswered

AG-02.name: Independent mentions
AG-02.finding_requires: the queries executed, each with its result count (zero allowed), and the identity the searches used; scoped to those searches

AG-03.name: Independent contradiction
AG-03.finding_requires: the exact site claim with its packet reference, an inspected conflicting page with URL and quote, why it is the same entity, date or context, and whether the conflict is material

AG-04.name: Facts drawn inside images
AG-04.finding_requires: an image candidate reference (I...) that was actually viewed, the fact transcribed from it, and why the page text does not state it

AG-05.name: Namesake ambiguity
AG-05.finding_requires: the competing entities observed, each with a URL and the fact that distinguishes it from the brand

AG-06.name: Review and profile opportunity
AG-06.finding_requires: the platform queries executed, why the platforms fit the business, and which platforms showed no matching profile
